verdict.biggest_gap: A's entire bottom third is a carpet of identical grass-tuft sprites at one scale, one hue and one density, spread edge-to-edge with no clumping, no worn path toward the lit castle, and no response to the moon light (tufts under the tree and in the ground's dark patches are exactly as bright as tufts in the open), so the foreground reads as a scattered asset layer sitting on a flat plane rather than terrain, and it drags the whole frame toward 'low-poly asset pack' even though the fog tiers and warm castle focal point behind it are doing real work.
verdict.fix: Drive the grass through a noise-based density and scale mask (0.6x-1.4x, 30-40% coverage instead of 100%), thin it to near-zero along a trodden path from the character toward the castle, tint the tufts by the terrain's lighting so they darken under the tree and in shadow patches and pick up a slight cool rim on the moon-facing side, and scatter a few larger grass/heather clumps and small rocks to break the uniform height line.
verdict.notes: B's framing arch of the giant root, the path leading through the character to the distant waterfall and ruins, and its restrained dark-blue-and-gold palette read as one deliberate, signature art direction rather than an assembled scene.

verdict.biggest_gap: B's environment reads as untextured blockout: the ground is a single flat dirt-coloured plane whose only value variation is the campfire's radial glow, littered with flat dark polygon "debris" that has no shading or AO, and the tents behind are flat-shaded boxes with hairline guy-ropes. Neither fighter casts a readable contact shadow (only dust puffs), so both characters float on a greybox rather than standing in a world, and the tents' scale relative to the figures is unanchored.
verdict.fix: Replace the flat ground plane with a splat-mapped trampled-dirt/gravel/grass material (albedo + normal, 2-3 vertex-painted layers with darkening under the fire and near tent edges), swap the scattered flat polygons for a handful of real props (rocks, a log, grass-tuft decals) with baked AO, and add soft capsule/blob contact shadows under both fighters so they sit on the surface.
verdict.notes: A is a fully coherent hand-painted art direction: one warm terracotta palette across architecture, props and characters, consistent stylized material language, and a clean diagonal composition (airborne enemy upper-left vs. grounded axe-wielder lower-right) with both silhouettes separated from the background and grounded by contact shadows.

verdict.biggest_gap: B's boundary wall is a flat additive blue card that has no lighting relationship with the world in front of it: the ground stays one uniform olive flat-shade, the grey rocks at the wall's base pick up zero blue tint, the character has no blue rim and no contact shadow, and the right-hand tree is pure unlit black. The wall therefore reads as a 2D backdrop pasted behind the geometry rather than a volumetric energy wall standing in the same scene, and the hard horizontal seam where the card meets the terrain is fully exposed.
verdict.fix: Make the ring emit light: place a chain of blue point/area lights along the inner edge of the wall (or a single wide directional fill aimed inward) with falloff over roughly 30-40m so rocks, terrain facets and the character's back/shoulder rim visibly take blue, then add a low height-based blue ground-fog band (2-3m tall) at the wall's base so the terrain fades into the wall instead of meeting it at a hard seam, and drop a soft blob/contact shadow under the character so it grounds.
verdict.notes: A's boundary actually participates in the scene's lighting: grass blades catch the glow, trees carry blue rim light, bounce fills the midground and volumetric haze softens the edge, so the wall feels physically present rather than composited.

verdict.biggest_gap: In A the grace paints a saturated orange pool on the ground but the player standing inside that pool receives almost none of it: the cape stays flat, unlit navy with no warm wrap or rim on the side facing the pillar, there is no cast shadow stretching toward the camera and no contact darkening under the feet, so the character reads as a sprite layered over a glow decal rather than a body standing in the light. The low-poly terrain faceting compounds it, but the light/character disconnect is the failure specific to this piece.
verdict.fix: Replace the ground-glow decal with a real shadow-casting warm point light at the pillar base (roughly #FFB95A, ~8m range, inverse-square falloff, shadow map on) so the player casts a long shadow toward the camera and gets a warm rim along the cape edges and pauldrons; add a soft AO/contact blob under the feet and let the same light drive a mild normal response on the terrain so the facets catch it unevenly instead of one flat orange wash.
verdict.notes: B's grace, fog, bounce and surface specular all obey one lighting model, so the gold column reads as an object sitting in a real room with depth and scale instead of an effect pasted over the scene.
